headlines.article_text: Comcast (CMCSA) earnings Q3 2026 Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Comcast topped analyst earnings expectations for the third quarter. Streaming service Peacock hit profitability for the second consecutive quarter. Comcast is in the process of spinning off its media business into a separate publicly traded company. Theme parks and the connectivity business continued to face pressure. In this article CMCSA Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT The Comcast corporate logo sits at the top of 30 Rock in Rockefeller Center, on August 19, 2026, in New York City. Gary Hershorn | Corbis News | Getty Images Comcast beat Wall Street's expectations for third-quarter earnings — despite headwinds in its theme parks business — thanks to continued strength in its media unit. The company's Peacock streaming service reported a quarterly profit for the second time since its launch in 2020, posting $261 million in adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization on $1.8 billion in revenue. The streaming platform continued to reap the benefits of record-high viewership for the FIFA World Cup, as the final games played out at the beginning of the quarter and aired on NBCUniversal's Telemundo and on Peacock. Revenue in Comcast's media division, which includes the streaming service, rose 13% compared with the third quarter last year to $5.4 billion. The overall content and experiences unit, which also includes its film studio and theme parks, saw revenue rise 6.5%. Comcast's connectivity and platforms sector, however, continued to face pressure, with revenue down 2.7% year over year. The company reported a net loss in domestic broadband residential customers of 144,000 and a net loss in its cable customers of 274,000 during the period. Its mobile business added 368,000 customers. After years of stagnating growth in broadband and heightened competition from wireless providers like Verizon and T-Mobile, Comcast announced in January 2025 that it would refocus on its mobile business and pursue more competitive pricing plans. Here's how Comcast performed for the period ended Sept. 30 compared with what analysts expected, according to LSEG: Earnings per share: $1.07 adjusted vs. 98 cents expected Revenue: $29.3 billion vs. $29.28 billion expected In June, Comcast announced plans to spin off NBCUniversal and European media business Sky from its core cable, wireless and business services units. The split, which Comcast said would take about a year, will create two separate publicly traded companies. Co-CEO and Chair Brian Roberts said on a call with investors directly following the June announcement that the separation would allow each business to have more "dedicated focus, strategic flexibility, and tailored investment priorities." The decision comes after Comcast spun off most of its cable networks , along with an array of digital businesses, into Versant . That separation was completed in January. For the third quarter, Comcast's revenue was 6% lower than the year-ago period. However, adjusting for the impact of the Versant spin, revenue was essentially flat year over year, Comcast said. Net income for the period was $3.45 billion, or 97 cents per share, compared with $3.33 billion, or 90 cents per share, in the third quarter of 2025. Adjusting for one-time items, including investments and the value of certain intangible assets, Comcast reported adjusted earnings per share of $1.07. The company's theme park revenue fell 4.4% during the period to $2.6 billion, which the company attributed to "cyclical headwinds" and lower revenue from admissions, dented by promotional activity. Adjusted EBITDA for the division sank 17%. The weakness in theme parks comes despite continued investment in the sector with the opening of a new coaster at Universal Studios Hollywood this quarter and Universal's largest theme park property, Epic Universe, last year. Theme park rival Disney reported record quarterly revenue in its park division in August. Disclosure: Versant Media Group is the parent company of CNBC. Kevin Carter | Getty Images Procter & Gamble on Thursday reported quarterly earnings and revenue that beat analysts' expectations, fueled by growing demand for its laundry detergent and home care products. Shares of the company rose more than 2% in premarket trading. Here's what the company reported compared with what Wall Street was expecting, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG: Earnings per share: $2.00 adjusted vs. $1.88 expected Revenue: $23.3 billion vs. $22.8 billion expected P&G reported fiscal first-quarter net income attributable to the company of $4.73 billion, or $1.97 per share, down from $4.75 billion, or $1.95 per share, a year earlier. Excluding restructuring costs and other items, the company earned $2 per share. Net sales rose 4% to $23.3 billion. P&G reported volume growth of 2.4%, a strong start for its new fiscal year. Like many consumer companies, P&G has seen demand for its products weaken as shoppers have become more value conscious. Executives have previously said that consumers are now using every last drop of shampoo or laundry detergent, and value packs have become more popular. In fiscal 2026, P&G reported just one quarter of volume growth. P&G's top performing division was fabric and home care, which includes brands like Tide and Febreze. The segment's volume rose 4.3% in the quarter. The company's baby, feminine and family care segment and its beauty business both reported volume growth of more than 2%. P&G's grooming division saw volume shrink 0.4% in the quarter. The segment includes Gillette and Venus razors. The company's health care business was the laggard of the portfolio this quarter. Its volume fell 2.9% as demand for oral health care products, like Crest toothpaste, and personal health care items, like Pepto-Bismol, shrank. The company is expecting continued "geopolitical and economic challenges," but P&G is on track to meet its guidance, CEO Shailesh Jejurikar said in a statement. For fiscal 2027, P&G reiterated its forecast for core earnings per share in a range of $6.89 to $7.11. The company is now projecting all-in sales growth in the range of 2% to 4% compared with the prior year, up from its prior outlook of 1% to 3%. headlines.article_text: Stocks making the biggest moves premarket: TSLA, META, AVEX, SPOT Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Check out the companies making the biggest moves premarket: Aevex — The defense company rose more than 11% after it disputed a Bloomberg News report that said the U.S. Navy would no longer buy Aevex's GARC boat drone due to performance issues. In a release, Aevex said " no orders have been halted ." Lockheed Martin — Shares rose 3% after the defense giant reported better-than-expected results for the third quarter. Lockheed also hiked its earnings and revenue guidance for 2026. Spotify — The audio streaming service gained 5% on fourth-quarter revenue guidance that exceeded analyst expectations. Spotify also said monthly active users rose 11% to 788 million year over year . Energy stocks — The group rose broadly as oil prices surged on renewed geopolitical fears . Kinder Morgan climbed nearly 2%, while APA , Valero Energy and ConocoPhillips advanced more than 1% each. Tesla — Elon Musk's auto manufacturer shed earlier gains and last traded down 3%. Tesla posted beats on the top and bottom lines in the third quarter . The company earned 48 cents per share on an adjusted basis and posted revenue of $28.05 billion. Analysts polled by LSEG were looking for 43 cents a share and $27.88 billion. International Business Machines — Shares slipped 5%. The company reported adjusted earnings of $2.95 per share for the third quarter, compared to analysts polled by LSEG's expectations for $2.86 per share. Revenue also beat estimates, and IBM now expects free cash flow for full-year 2026 to increase by more than $1 billion over the year prior. Rollins — The pest control company saw shares fall more than 5% after third-quarter results missed the Street's estimates. Rollins earned 33 cents a share on $1.09 billion in revenue, while the FactSet consensus sought 34 cents a share and $1.11 billion. Meta Platforms — The social media giant slipped 2% even after revenue came in ahead of analysts' estimates. Third-quarter revenue of $64.60 billion topped the LSEG consensus call for $63.37 billion. The midpoint of its fourth-quarter sales guidance was also above the Street's estimates. CSX — The railway company gained 2% after third-quarter earnings beat expectations. CSX earned 57 cents per share on revenue of $4.02 billion, while analysts surveyed by LSEG called for 53 cents a share and $3.96 billion. Revenue per unit increased 7% in the period, compared to the StreetAccount consensus expectation for 5.9% growth. Las Vegas Sands – Shares of the resort company fell 2% after the company posted disappointing third-quarter results. Las Vegas Sands posted adjusted earnings of 54 cents per share on revenue of $3.22 billion. Analysts surveyed by LSEG were expecting 69 cents in earnings per share and $3.35 billion in revenue. Lam Research — The semiconductor manufacturing equipment company dropped more than 7%. Lam sees second-quarter adjusted earnings of $2.33 per share, plus or minus 15 cents, on revenue of $8.60 billion, plus or minus $400 million. That compares to analysts' expectation for $2.31 per share and revenue of $8.53 billion. QuantumScape – Shares of the company behind lithium-metal battery tech surged 7%. QuantumScape announced plans for a 100 megawatt-hour solid-state battery production line for artificial intelligence data centers. Molina Healthcare – The managed healthcare services provider dipped 3%. While third-quarter results beat expectations, premium revenue guidance for the full year is unchanged at roughly $42 billion. The company's guidance metrics across all segments are also reaffirmed. Molina president and CEO Joseph Zubretsky said, "With the apparent plateauing of medical cost trend, which remains at elevated levels, and the strength of recent rate updates for 2027, we believe we are likely observing the beginning of the turn in Medicaid margins." — CNBC's Davis Giangiulio, Sean Conlon, Sarah Min and Paulina Likos contributed reporting.
